project.objective: When and where did Umbelina Maria Azevedo die? She was the wife of Francisco Antônio Pariz and the mother of Alice Umbelina, Antônio Francisco, Maria Glória, Florita Umbelina and Maura Umbelina, born between about 1902 and 1918, several of them in Espírito Santo.

researcher_profile.narration_guidance: Plain language for someone who has never done genealogy. No identifiers, file names, tool names or field names. Never write GPS, proof, proved or exhaustive: say genealogy standards; call an answer a conclusion when it is well established and a finding otherwise; say what we searched and what we could not reach. Do not describe your own instructions or checks. Do not narrate between actions; report once when the step is done: what was found, in one paragraph, and what happens next in one sentence.

questions.question: When and where did Umbelina Maria Azevedo, wife of Francisco Antônio Pariz and mother of children born about 1902–1918 in Espírito Santo, die?
questions.rationale: This is the project's sole objective restated with identifying detail. Umbelina has a Death fact on the tree with no date or place. Her children all died in Rio de Janeiro in the mid-twentieth century and their death records from the Rio de Janeiro civil registration collection name her as mother, establishing her presence in that state. Civil registration records for Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo — the two states where the family is documented — are available on FamilySearch and are the logical starting point.

items.rationale: Collection 1582573 (Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Civil Registration, 1804-2013) is name-searchable and covers both the city of Rio de Janeiro (Federal District 1834–1960, Guanabara state 1960–1975) and the state under a single search interface, per loc_001. All five children died in Rio de Janeiro between 1971 and 1990, making Rio de Janeiro the highest-probability jurisdiction for Umbelina's death. Search for death (óbitos) records under both her maiden name — Azevedo, de Azevedo — and her married name — Pariz, Paris, Parez — as the loc_001 guide notes explicitly that women's death records may be filed under the married name. Existing children's death records name her as 'Umbelina Maria Azevedo', 'Umbelina Maria de Azevedo', and 'Umbelina Maria Pariz de Azevedo', confirming both forms appear. Date range 1920–1990 spans from the year after her last known child was born (Maura, 1918) through the death of her oldest surviving child (Alice, 1990).

FAN item: Francisco Antônio Pariz (husband, GXSQ-FYP) has a Death fact in the tree with no date or place. His five existing sources are all children's death records naming him as father — his own death record has not been found. Search collection 1582573 (name-searchable) for his death under all surname variants (Pariz, Paris, Parez, Páris). His death record is a FAN source bearing directly on Umbelina's death question: if he predeceased her, the record may note a surviving widow; if she predeceased him, his record may name her as the deceased spouse. Either outcome narrows the window for Umbelina's death or confirms a jurisdiction. Date range 1920–1990 covers his plausible death window given children born 1902–1918.

Collection 1719212 (Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Catholic Church Records, 1616-2017) is name-searchable. Per loc_001, civil registration compliance in some municipalities was uneven through the early 1920s; a Catholic burial register entry may record Umbelina's death even in the absence of a civil record. Search for burial (sepultamentos or óbitos) under both name forms (Azevedo / Pariz). This item is a fallback if collection 1582573 yields no civil death record for Umbelina.

Collection 2137269 (Brazil, Cemetery Records, 1799-2024) is name-searchable. A cemetery burial record for Umbelina would supply a death date and burial location, and could be cross-referenced against the civil and church results. Search under maiden name Azevedo and married name Pariz. This item is a fallback if the church burial search (pli_003) also yields nothing.

Collection 4426177 (Brazil, Espírito Santo, Church Records, 1821-2000) is name-searchable. The Pariz family was in Espírito Santo at least through 1915 (Florita born there); no dedicated Espírito Santo civil registration collection was returned by collections_search. If Umbelina died in Espírito Santo before or during the migration to Rio de Janeiro, her death would appear in a parish burial register there. No Espírito Santo civil registration collection was found on FamilySearch, so Catholic church records are the primary available source for that state. Search under maiden name Azevedo and married name Pariz. Date range 1900–1960 brackets the family's Espírito Santo period through a plausible late migration date. This item is a fallback if the Rio de Janeiro searches (pli_001, pli_003, pli_004) yield nothing.

Collection 4473668 (Brazil, Espírito Santo, Civil Registration, 1850-2019) is name-searchable. Prior item pli_005 searched only Espírito Santo Catholic church records (collection 4426177) under the incorrect assumption that no civil registration collection existed for that state on FamilySearch; the FamilySearch wiki confirms collection 4473668 is available and fully indexed. The Pariz family was in Espírito Santo at least through 1915 (Florita born there), making Espírito Santo a plausible jurisdiction for Umbelina's death if she died before or during the family's migration to Rio de Janeiro. Search for death (óbitos) records under both the maiden name (Azevedo, de Azevedo) and the married name (Pariz, Paris, Parez), and with husband Francisco Pariz as a spouse anchor. Date range 1900–1960 spans the family's confirmed Espírito Santo presence through a plausible late-migration date.

Ancestry collection 9799 (Brazil Civil Registration, 1870–2012) is name-searchable and covers civil registration records nationally, including both Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro under a single search. This item was deferred during execution of the prior plan. A national-scope Ancestry search may surface civil records under Umbelina's name that FamilySearch's collection-specific searches did not return, due to differences in indexing coverage or transcription. Search under maiden name Azevedo and married name Pariz; also search husband Francisco Pariz as a spouse anchor. Date range 1920–1990 covers the full plausible death window from after the last child's birth (~1918) through the death of the last surviving child (Alice, 1990). This item is a fallback if collection 4473668 (pli_006) yields nothing in Espírito Santo.
items.skip_reason: Ancestry (collection 9799, Brazil Civil Registration 1870-2012) requires a paid subscription and human browser access; automated search tools cannot execute this item. The researcher should open https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9799/ and search for death records under: (1) surname Azevedo, given name Umbelina Maria, death 1920-1990, country Brazil; (2) surname Pariz, given name Umbelina, death 1920-1990, country Brazil; (3) given name Umbelina, spouse surname Pariz, death 1920-1990, country Brazil. No prior search was ever logged against this item (contrary to a suggestion that log_035 covered it — log_035 does not exist in the log for any pli associated with q_001). The primary item pli_006 returned negative, so the fallback condition is met; this item should be executed by the researcher before research-exhaustiveness declares the plan complete.

items.repository: Hemeroteca Digital Nacional (Biblioteca Nacional Digital, hemerotecadigital.bn.gov.br)
items.rationale: Search for death notices or obituaries for Umbelina Maria Azevedo (alive as of December 1978 per Maura's death record) in Rio de Janeiro newspapers including Jornal do Brasil, O Globo, and Correio da Manhã. Death notices were commonly published in Rio de Janeiro papers throughout this period. A notice would supply a death date, place and possibly surviving family members. Date range begins 1978 — the year Maura died and Umbelina was last confirmed alive — and extends to 2000 to cover the full plausible window. This item covers the Hemeroteca Digital gap identified by the exhaustiveness agent.
items.skip_reason: Hemeroteca Digital Nacional (hemerotecadigital.bn.gov.br) is free but bot-protected; automated search tools cannot execute this item. The build_external_search_url tool classified it as free_bot_protected. URLs were generated for the researcher to use manually in a browser — log_049 (https://hemerotecadigital.bn.gov.br/acervo-digital?q=Umbelina+Azevedo+falecimento) and log_051 (https://hemerotecadigital.bn.gov.br/acervo-digital?q=Umbelina+Pariz+falecimento) — both returned with captureReceived: false. With pli_007 (Ancestry) also skipped as inaccessible, all remaining unsearched sources require human browser access and the nothing_further_reachable exception applies.

query.request: check children's death records for any notation that Umbelina was deceased at time of filing, or any death date/place for her

log.notes:
SOURCES CHECKED: Umbelina Maria Azevedo (GXSQ-V3L) — five children's death records read, ten record personas examined

All five children's death records from Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Civil Registration, 1804-2013 (collection 1582573) were read — both the child's own indexed persona and Umbelina's separate persona from the same record. Every record names Umbelina as the mother.

What each record shows in the index:

1. Antônio Francisco Pariz — died 7 September 1971, Cascadura, Rio de Janeiro. Umbelina indexed as "Umbelina Maria Azevedo," mother. No facts (birth, death, or deceased-status) indexed for her. Note: the father is indexed as "Francisco Antonio Azevedo" — surname Azevedo rather than Pariz — which is anomalous and may reflect an indexer's reading of an unusual notation in the original.

2. Maura Umbelina Ferreira — died 19 December 1978, Duque de Caxias. Umbelina indexed as "Umbelina Maria de Azevedo," mother. No facts indexed for her.

3. Florita Umbelina dos Santos — died 2 July 1980, Rio de Janeiro. Umbelina indexed as "Umbelina Maria Pariz de Azevedo," mother. No facts indexed for her.

4. Maria Glória Ferreira — died 17 May 1982, Rio de Janeiro. Umbelina indexed as "Umbelina Maria de Azevedo," mother. No facts indexed for her.

5. Alice Umbelina dos Santos — died 7 April 1990, Rio de Janeiro. Umbelina indexed as "Umbelina Maria de Azevedo," mother. No facts indexed for her.

Conclusion: The FamilySearch index for this collection does not capture the alive/deceased status of parents listed in death registrations. The "falecido/a" (deceased) or "vivo/a" (living) notation that a Brazilian civil registration clerk would write beside a parent's name is not extracted as a structured data field. None of the five indexed records therefore carries any death fact or deceased-status for Umbelina, not because she was necessarily alive at the time but because the indexers did not capture that field.

The original page images are available for all five registrations and are the only way to read any parent-status notation. Those images are linked to each registration and can be opened on FamilySearch. Opening them is the next step to answer whether any of these records notes Umbelina as deceased, and if so, which is the earliest record to do so — that would give an upper-bound date for her death.

Mother Umbelina Maria Azevedo named on record (p_113204041100). Father indexed as Francisco Antonio Azevedo — possible indexing error, original image needed. imageArk: ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-62Y3-ZW5.

Antônio Francisco Pariz death record, Cascadura, 8 September 1971. Mother listed as 'Umbelina Maria Azevo-do' with NO qualifier (neither 'dona' nor 'falecida'). The absence of a qualifier is ambiguous — Brazilian registrars of this era were inconsistent in applying alive/deceased markers. This record does not confirm or deny Umbelina's survival in September 1971.

Maria Glória Ferreira (born Pariz) death record, Rio de Janeiro city, 17 May 1982. Mother listed as 'Umbelina Maria de Azevedo' with NO qualifier. Father surname misspelled 'Faria' instead of 'Pariz' — scribal error confirmed by all sibling records consistently showing 'Pariz'. No alive/deceased marker for Umbelina.

Alice Umbelina dos Santos (born Pariz) death record, Duque de Caxias, 7 April 1990. Mother listed as 'Umbelina Maria de Cezevedo' [scribal spelling error for Azevedo] with NO qualifier. Alice's birth year given as 1890 (age 88 at death). No alive/deceased marker for Umbelina. Combined with Maura's 1978 record (which uses 'dona Umbelina' — a positive alive marker), the pattern across all FAN records shows: one explicit alive marker in 1978; three records (1971, 1982, 1990) without any qualifier. The absence of 'falecida' in the 1982 and 1990 records weakly corroborates survival past December 1978, but Brazilian registrar inconsistency means this cannot be relied upon as proof of life.

Ancestry collection 9799 (Brazil Civil Registration, 1870-2012) covers both Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro in a single national search and may have different indexing than the FamilySearch per-state collections. Three strategies to run manually: (1) Surname Azevedo, given name Umbelina Maria, death 1920-1990; (2) Surname Pariz, given name Umbelina, death 1920-1990; (3) Given name Umbelina, spouse Francisco Pariz, death 1920-1990. A positive result would provide death date, municipality, and cartório reference — the core answer to q_001. No automated access available; researcher must run this manually on ancestry.com with a paid subscription.

quirks: Civil registration is recorded at the municipal (cartório) level — search municipality by municipality; for the city of Rio de Janeiro, separate offices (circunscrições) served different neighborhoods, so searching office by office is necessary when the home neighborhood is unknown.

The city of Rio de Janeiro was a separate Federal District from 1834 to 1960 and NOT part of the State of Rio de Janeiro; FamilySearch collection 1582573 covers both the city and state records together under one search interface.

From April 1960 to 1975, deaths in the city of Rio de Janeiro were recorded under the State of Guanabara, not the State of Rio de Janeiro — deaths in the city after April 1960 require searching Guanabara records.
Death records for women may be filed under the married name — the FamilySearch wiki for the Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Civil Registration collection states this explicitly.

Civil registration compliance was uneven: the Brazil Civil Registration wiki page states that while the Catholic Church was required to keep records from 1850, justices of the peace took over from 1870, and some municipalities did not begin keeping records until as recently as the 1920s — if no civil death record is found before approximately 1920, search Catholic burial registers.
Records are in Portuguese: 'Óbitos' = deaths, 'Nascimentos' = births, 'Casamentos' or 'Matrimônios' = marriages, 'Índice' = index.

Volume_search returned 11,500 digitized death-record volumes for Rio de Janeiro 1900–1960; all 100 examined on the first page show recordSearchablePercent: 100 (fully name-indexed); the indexed collection-level search in collection 1582573 should be the first step before browsing individual volumes.

There is a neighborhood named 'Espírito Santo' in the city of Rio de Janeiro — FamilySearch death-record volumes labeled 'Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil' are from that city district, not from the state of Espírito Santo.

Women in Brazil historically retained their maiden surname; from the late 19th century it became common to adopt the husband's surname, but either form may appear in records — search both the maiden name (Azevedo) and the married name (Pariz or Páris) when looking for Umbelina's death record.
Some civil registration books have indexes in the front or back organized by given name only — if searching a volume manually, check every entry under 'U' (Umbelina) rather than under the surname.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil (1900–1960)
## Focus: Civil Registration Death Records

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** The captaincy and later province of Rio de Janeiro dates from 1565; became a state under the republic in 1889.
- **Administrative center:** Niterói was the state capital throughout this period; the city of Rio de Janeiro was a separate Federal District.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Federal Republic of Brazil
- **Population during period:** Estimates for Rio de Janeiro state range from roughly 900,000–1,157,000 in 1900 to approximately 3.3–3.4 million by 1960 (populstat.info estimates via FamilySearch place population data). Brazil's national population grew from about 17.9 million (1900) to 72.4 million (1960).
- **Economy:** Coffee cultivation (inland zones), sugar (Campos region), early industrialization (Petrópolis), commerce and port trade (capital city).
- **Ethnic composition:** Mixed Portuguese-descended population, significant African-descended population, Italian and German immigrant communities, and internal migrants from Espírito Santo, Minas Gerais, and the Northeast.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic throughout the period; smaller Methodist, Presbyterian, Baptist, and Lutheran congregations also present.
- **Key historical events:** Abolition of slavery (1888), proclamation of the Republic (1889), transfer of the national capital from the city of Rio de Janeiro to Brasília (April 1960).

## Boundary changes
- **City / State split (1834–1975):** From 1834 the city of Rio de Janeiro was carved out as a separate Federal District and was NOT part of the State of Rio de Janeiro. This means deaths occurring within the city limits during 1900–1960 were registered under the city's own civil registration offices, not the state's.
- **State of Guanabara (1960–1975):** When the federal capital moved to Brasília in April 1960, the old Federal District became the new State of Guanabara. Deaths in the city of Rio de Janeiro from April 1960 onward are in Guanabara records, not State of Rio de Janeiro records.
- **1975 merger:** Guanabara was merged back into the State of Rio de Janeiro; the combined FamilySearch collection 1582573 covers both entities and can be searched as one.
- **State boundaries otherwise stable** throughout 1900–1960.
- Many towns in Rio de Janeiro are relatively new; if no records are found for a specific municipality, determine when it was founded and which older municipality it was split from, then search the parent municipality's records.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date and level:** A national law passed in 1850 required registration of births and deaths; until 1870 the Catholic Church kept these records for the government; from 1870 justices of the peace took over at the **municipal level**. The [Brazil Civil Registration wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Civil_Registration) states that compliance was uneven and some municipalities did not begin keeping records until the 1920s.
- **What exists for 1900–1960:** Births (nascimentos), marriages (casamentos), and deaths (óbitos) at the municipal cartório level across all municipalities of the state and the city of Rio de Janeiro. FamilySearch collection [Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Civil Registration, 1804–2013](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1582573) holds 6,328,974 indexed records representing 58,567,999 persons with 5,100,470 images — the principal searchable database for this period.
- **Death record content:** Per the [FamilySearch collection wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil,_Rio_de_Janeiro,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records): name of informant; date, place, and time of death; name, gender, and age of deceased; nationality, state of birth, and residence; cause of death; parents' names and residence; names of witnesses; burial place.
- **Where held:** Originals held by the Corregedoria Geral da Justiça do Estado do Rio de Janeiro and local cartórios; the Arquivo Nacional do Brasil (Rio de Janeiro) holds some duplicate sets (1929–1962 in collection olib:1928224). FamilySearch has digitized and indexed most volumes.
- **Gaps:** Some municipalities with very small populations may have sparse or late-starting records. The city of Rio de Janeiro's records before 1960 require searching under the Federal District designation, though collection 1582573 encompasses them.
- **Pre-registration alternative:** Catholic burial registers (see Church records below).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (overwhelmingly dominant); smaller Protestant congregations.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (batismos), marriages (matrimônios), burials (óbitos/sepultamentos), confirmations. The [Brazil Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Church_Records) notes that Catholic burial registers include the deceased's name, date and place of death or burial, age, residence, cause of death, survivors, and parents' names.
- **Online collection:** [Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Catholic Church Records, 1616–2017](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1719212) — 2,282,412 indexed records, 11,107,767 persons, 368,464 images. This collection covers the 1900–1960 period. The [Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Genealogy wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro,_Brazil_Genealogy) advises searching both civil and church records because each may contain information absent from the other: church records often list godparents where civil records list grandparents.
- **Where held:** Earlier records may be at the diocese; more recent records at local parish offices. The Archdiocese of São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro covers the capital city. Use [The Catholic Directory: Brazil](https://www.catholicdirectory.com/brazil) to locate parish contact information.
- **Language:** Portuguese; Latin terms appear in older sacramental entries.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** Brazil took national censuses in 1900, 1920, 1940, 1950, and 1960. The [Brazil Census wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Census) states that after compiling statistical information, the original census returns in Brazil were often destroyed. No FamilySearch indexed census collection for Rio de Janeiro state from this period appeared in the survey results.
- **Substitute enumerations:** The Brazil Census wiki notes that some ecclesiastical census records survive in diocesan archives. City directories for Rio de Janeiro city may substitute for census years to place a person at a specific address.
- **Access:** The national census schedules that do survive are held at regional archives and require in-person visits or correspondence.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testamentos), administrations (inventários), guardianships, estate distributions.
- **Where held:** The FamilySearch Catalog returned 349 hits for Rio de Janeiro, including notarial records, court records, and civil registration books held by the Corregedoria Geral da Justiça. The [Brazil Online Genealogy Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Online_Genealogy_Records) lists [Inventários e Testamentos](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/95936) at FamilySearch (images only).
- **Practical value for this project:** Probate records could name Umbelina as a deceased parent if one of her children initiated an estate proceeding; however, civil death records are the primary target.

### Land records
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Brazil Wiki notes land and property records exist but these are not the primary record type for this project. The [Brazil Land and Property wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Land_and_Property) covers deeds and notarial records.
- **Where held:** Cartórios de registro de imóveis at the municipal level.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Brazil participated in World War I (limited) and World War II (1942–1945). Brazilian military draft registration and service records exist.
- **Where held:** The Arquivo Nacional (https://www.gov.br/arquivonacional/pt-br) holds federal military records. Not a primary target for this project.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** [Brazil, Cemetery Records, 1799–2024](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2137269) — 2,748,601 indexed records, 14,765,819 persons, 150,972 images. This is a national collection covering Rio de Janeiro cemeteries.
- **Additional resources:** [BillionGraves](https://billiongraves.com/search/results?year_range=5&action=search_cemetery&exact=true&country=Brazil) and [FindAGrave](https://findagrave.com/cgi-bin/fg.cgi?page=csr&CScn=&CScntry=20&CSst=0) provide Brazil cemetery memorials.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers at local cemetery offices and associated churches.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Context for this project:** Umbelina's family migrated internally from Espírito Santo to Rio de Janeiro state; these are internal migrants, not international immigrants. However, immigration cards cover arrivals into the port of Rio de Janeiro.
- **Online collection:** [Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Immigration Cards, 1900–1980](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1932363) — 6,193,545 persons, 3,967,834 images. Also at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9800/) and [MyHeritage](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30284/brazil-rio-de-janeiro-immigration-cards-1900-1965).
- **Port records:** The Arquivo Nacional holds [Entrada de Estrangeiros no Brasil, Port of Rio de Janeiro](https://bases.an.gov.br/rv/menu_externo/menu_externo.php).
- **Internal migration:** No dedicated FamilySearch collection for internal Brazilian migration records was found in this survey.

### Naturalization records
- Naturalization and foreigner registration records appear in: [Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, processos de naturalização e outros registros de imigração, 1897–1980](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/3277132) (FamilySearch Catalog — images). Also [Brazil, Foreigner Files, 1653–2022](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/5000160) — 3,512,065 persons. Relevant only if Umbelina or her husband Francisco Antônio Pariz was foreign-born.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The city of Rio de Janeiro had multiple major newspapers throughout this period (Jornal do Brasil, O Globo, Correio da Manhã). Obituaries and death notices were commonly published.
- **Online access:** [Acervo - Estadão](http://acervo.estadao.com.br/) and [Acervo Folha de São Paulo](http://acervo.folha.com.br/) are digitized newspaper archives. The Biblioteca Nacional Digital Brasil holds historical Rio de Janeiro newspapers.
- **Value:** Obituaries may name surviving children and parents, giving the date and municipality of death.

### Tax records
- No FamilySearch indexed tax collection specific to Rio de Janeiro 1900–1960 was found in this survey. Tax records are held at the state and municipal archive level.

**Coverage of this survey:** Volume_search returned 11,500 total digitized death-record volumes matching Rio de Janeiro state and 1900–1960; the 100 volumes detailed on the first page cover localities including the city of Rio de Janeiro (1937–1941+), Irajá (1921–1959), São João de Meriti (1941–1961), Itaperuna (1933–1951), Petrópolis (1902–1930), and others. All showed recordSearchablePercent: 100 (fully name-indexed). The remaining approximately 11,400 volumes were not examined — use the name-search in collection 1582573 first.

## Records NOT online
- Brazilian national census original returns for 1900, 1920, 1940, 1950, 1960 — mostly destroyed or held only at regional archives, not digitized on FamilySearch.
- Many Catholic parish burial registers not yet included in collection 1719212.
- Cartório death records for some smaller municipalities that have not yet been digitized (check the FamilySearch Catalog for the specific municipality).
- City directory (almanak / anuário) records for Rio de Janeiro city — useful to establish address before and after a death; held at the Biblioteca Nacional and accessible in-person.

## Known record losses
- The Brazil Census wiki states that most original census returns were destroyed after statistical compilation — this is a known, system-wide loss, not a localized disaster.
- No courthouse fires or flood losses specific to Rio de Janeiro state civil registration for 1900–1960 were identified in the sources consulted in this survey; however, individual cartórios may have suffered localized losses not captured here.

## Research tips
- **Start with the indexed collection.** The [Brazil, Rio de Janeiro, Civil Registration, 1804–2013](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1582573) collection is searchable by name and covers the full 1900–1960 target period for both the city and the state. Search Umbelina's name in both her maiden form (Azevedo) and her married form (Pariz or Páris), since the [FamilySearch collection wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil,_Rio_de_Janeiro,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records) explicitly notes that a woman's death record may be filed under her married name.
- **Search both civil and church records.** The [Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro,_Brazil_Genealogy) advises that church records may contain information absent from civil records and vice versa; search collection 1719212 (Catholic church records) alongside 1582573.
- **Municipal-level geography matters.** Per the [Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro,_Brazil_Genealogy): civil registration is kept at the municipal level; if the exact municipality is unknown, search the collection by name first and use any resulting record to determine the municipality, then verify against the browsable images. In the city of Rio de Janeiro itself, multiple registration districts (circunscrições) existed — if the neighborhood is known, start with the nearest office's records.
- **City vs. state records.** Deaths occurring within the city of Rio de Janeiro during 1900–1960 were registered in the Federal District's own records (not the State's), but FamilySearch collection 1582573 encompasses both, so one search covers both. After April 1960, city deaths fall under the State of Guanabara.
- **Read record indexes carefully.** The [Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro,_Brazil_Genealogy) notes that some civil registration books have indexes organized by given name only — check every entry under 'U' (Umbelina) rather than relying solely on the surname index.
- **Search the children's death records for parent information.** Rio de Janeiro death records include the parents' names and residence. The children who died in Rio de Janeiro state are the most direct source for Umbelina's whereabouts and possibly her own death record.
- **Portuguese vocabulary.** 'Óbitos' = deaths, 'Nascimentos' = births, 'Casamentos'/'Matrimônios' = marriages, 'Índice' = index. The [Portugal Script Tutorial](https://script.byu.edu/portuguese-handwriting/introduction) and the [Portuguese Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portuguese_Genealogical_Word_List) (from the [Brazil Naming Customs wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Naming_Customs)) assist with reading handwritten records.
- **Neighborhood named 'Espírito Santo' in the city.** Volume records labeled 'Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil' on FamilySearch are from a city district, not from the state of Espírito Santo where the family was born.
- **Cemetery records as a cross-check.** Search [Brazil, Cemetery Records, 1799–2024](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2137269) and [FindAGrave Brazil](https://findagrave.com/cgi-bin/fg.cgi?page=csr&CScn=&CScntry=20&CSst=0) to corroborate a civil death date and identify burial location.
- **Writing to the cartório.** If a record is not yet online, the [Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro,_Brazil_Genealogy) provides guidance on writing to the local Cartório de Registro Civil in Portuguese; it notes this method is not always reliable. Use the [Portuguese Letter-writing Guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portuguese_Letter-writing_Guide) for drafting the request.
- **Compliance timeline.** The [Brazil Civil Registration wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Brazil_Civil_Registration) states that while the Catholic Church kept vital records from 1850, justices of the peace took over from 1870, and some municipalities did not begin until the 1920s — if the civil death record is not found, go to the Catholic burial register for the same municipality.
